context:
See the two Land Use Land Cover maps of Ichalkaranji city, Kolhapur district, given below and observe how changes have occurred in the city over the years. Map A) is for 2007 and map B) for 2017. Both are at a scale of 1:80,000 and were generated by the Maharashtra Remote Sensing Application Centre, Department of Planning, Government of Maharashtra.

The legend is:

| Colour | Land use / land cover class |
|---|---|
| Pale yellow | Agriculture |
| Olive green | Forest |
| Light pink (mauve) | Wasteland-Scrub |
| Blue | Waterbodies |
| Dark red | Built Up - Rural |
| Bright pink (magenta) | Built Up - Residential |
| Salmon | Built Up - Residential-Sparse |
| Navy blue | Built Up - Industrial |
| Purple | Built Up - Public/Semipublic |
| Dark green | Built Up - Recreation |
| Brown | Built Up - Mining/Quarry |
| Pale teal | Built Up - Open Space |

On both maps a blue line runs across the south-east corner, labelled PANCHAGANAGA RIVER, and a network of thin black lines crosses the map. The settlements named are Ichalkaranji, Rui, Chandur, Sajani, Korochi, Takawade, Ingali, Haroli, Jambhali, Nandani, Kondigre, Yadrav, Mangaonwadi, Gaon Bhag and Shahu Nagar, with two areas marked INDUSTRIAL ESTATE. Also labelled are a stadium, several colleges and gardens, a sports complex, a playground, temples, a bus stand, an S.T. depot, an RTO office, an MSEB power station, a water treatment plant and a sewrage treatment plant.

Between 2007 and 2017 the bright pink residential area of Ichalkaranji spreads outward in every direction, most of it over ground that was pale yellow agriculture or light pink wasteland-scrub on the earlier map. The navy blue industrial patches also grow, and a brown mining/quarry patch appears in the north-west.

Write a note in your own words about how land use in Lonar city has evolved over time.

Two Land Use Land Cover maps of Lonar city are given, one for 2005-06 and one for 2015-16, both at a scale of 1:30,000 and generated by the Maharashtra Remote Sensing Application Centre. Their legend is:

| Colour | Land use / land cover class |
|---|---|
| Pale yellow | Agriculture |
| Olive green | Forest |
| Light pink (mauve) | Wasteland-Scrub |
| Blue | Waterbodies |
| Dark red | Built Up - Rural |
| Bright pink (magenta) | Built Up - Residential |
| Salmon | Built Up - Residential-Sparse |
| Navy blue | Built Up - Industrial |
| Purple | Built Up - Public/Semipublic |
| Dark green | Built Up - Recreation |
| Brown | Built Up - Mining/Quarry |
| Pale teal | Built Up - Open Space |

On the 2005-06 map the features named are Lonar Lake with its ring of forest, Lonar City, Lonar, Saraswati Village, Lonai Village and two Temples.

On the 2015-16 map all of those still appear, and in addition Krishna Nagar, Central Public School, Civil & Criminal Court, Tehsil Office, Rural Hospital, Gov. Hostel and Gov. ITI are named. The bright pink residential area around Lonar City is larger, and a band of residential and sparse-residential land now extends south-east past Lonai Village towards Krishna Nagar over ground that was Wasteland-Scrub in 2005-06.

subtopic: Types of Urban Settlements and Their Functions
context:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow :

Different types of human settlements include hamlets, villages, small towns, large towns, isolated places, cities and conurbations. In some systems, types of human settlements are broken up into urban, suburban and rural; for example, the U.S. Census Bureau divides settlements into urban or rural categories based on precise definitions. Small settlements, such as hamlets and villages, have low populations and restricted access to services. Larger types of settlements, such as cities, have higher populations, higher densities and greater access to services. For example, a village may have only one or two general stores, while a large metropolis may have many specialized stores and chain stores. These differences are known as low-order service settlements and high-order service settlements. Larger settlements also have a sphere of influence affecting surrounding settlements. Settlements may also be divided by the site chosen, such as sites selected based on resources, trading points, defensive sites, shelter and relationship to water resources. The functions of human settlements also differ, as settlements may be established as ports, market towns and resorts. Types of rural settlements may also be classified by function, such as proximity to farming, fishing and mining. Settlements that focus on one economic activity are called single functional settlements. Human settlements may be permanent or temporary. For example, a refugee camp is a temporary settlement, while a city is a permanent settlement.
